changes.after: A block used with define_method can keep access to local values where the block was made.

before: define_method(:scale) installs an instance method using the supplied block. Its parameter value becomes the method argument, and the block can capture surrounding local bindings such as factor.

A normal def body does not capture the surrounding local variables in this way. define_method is useful for a small explicit family of behaviors; it does not require eval or executing strings from users. Repeated definitions of the same method name replace earlier definitions rather than creating argument-count overloads.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
class Calculator
  factor = 3
  define_method(:scale) do |value|
    value * factor
  end
end
puts Calculator.new.scale(4)
```
Expected output or behavior: 12. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
